title.narrative: Smallholder farmer household Dietary Diversity (disaggregated by gender).

description.narrative: Dietary diversity is a proxy measure of diet adequacy, specifically micronutrient adequacy. According to the Zambia FoodBased Dietary Guideline Technical Recommendations, an individual should eat food types from all the 6 food groups everyday to stay strong. Eating from all the six food groups contribute to the nutrition wellbeing of an individual and is associated with improved income and economic status of a household. This indicator is applied at household level. Computation: This indicator is measured using the Household Dietary Diversity Score (HDDS) by totaling the number of food groups consumed by members of the household.

title.narrative: Proportion of Smallholder farmers living below the national poverty line (disaggregated by farmer type, gender and agroecological region).

description.narrative: This indicator measures a smallholder farmer households standard of living using the national poverty line. The LCMS under Zamstats uses poverty lines comprising of two principal components: food and nonfood. The food poverty line represents the cost of a food bundle that provides 12,450 kcal per day, which are the necessary energy requirements for a family of six people or 4.52 adult equivalents. Computation: Zamstats standard measure of the poverty lines will be applied to establish the gap.

title.narrative: Number of smallholder farmers with knowledge of recommended SIP packages and climate change adaptation measures (disaggregated by gender of farmer)

description.narrative: This indicator tracks the progress in transferring knowledge of SIPs and climate change to targeted 43,000 farmers through training, mentoring, extension services and peer to peer. Specifically, the indicator will monitor the number of farmers that are trained and mentored in recommended SIP packages released by the project research activities and they demonstrate the knowledge of these SIPs. Further, it will track farmers trained in climate change adaptation measures. Computation: Cumulative number of farmers with knowledge of SIP packages recommended by the SIFAZ project and climate change adaptation. Given that the SIP packages are recommended by farming system and ecology, this computation will avoid double counting of the targeted farmers.

title.narrative: Annual gross margin ZMW/ha, real values from crop production by smallholder farmers under SIFAZ (calculated in maizebased farming system, disaggregated AER gender

description.narrative: The gross margin (calculated per hectare) will be used to indicate crop production profitability by smallholder farmers. Gross margin generally refers to the remaining income from an enterprise after the variable costs are deducted. The variable cost of production included here are the costs of seeds, labour, chemicals (herbicides & pesticides) and fertilizers. This indicator is disaggregated by crop in a farming system. The gross margins will be monitored for production of maize and cassava farming systems. Computation. Gross Margin for Maize/Cassava (ZMW/ha) ((Yield (kg/ha) x Price (ZMW/kg)) Variable cost (ZMW/ha). Value calculated for each gender and deflated to real values by prevailing Consumer Price Index (CPI)

The variable cost of production included here are the costs of seeds, labour, chemicals (herbicides & pesticides) and fertilizers. This indicator is disaggregated by crop in a farming system. The gross margins will be monitored for production of maize and cassava farming systems. Computation. Gross Margin for Maize/Cassava (ZMW/ha) ((Yield (kg/ha) x Price (ZMW/kg)) Variable cost (ZMW/ha). Value calculated for each gender and deflated to real values by prevailing Consumer Price Index (CPI)

Value will be calculated for each gender of farmer household SIP package goes beyond conservation agriculture principle and demonstrates achievement of results against SIP parameters defined by the project.
